thread:
Alex: noticed apiserver connection spike in eu-central ~17:25 UTC, connection count jumped ~1200 in 2min and p99 latency to etcd climbed. kv-cache miss rate doubled.
SRE Bot: alert: apiserver.conn_count > 1000 (eu-central) — paging on-call
Maria: any obvious deploys around that time? metrics point to lots of short-lived connections.
Alex: no user deploys. correlates with a large GPU onboarding batch from provisioning pipeline — many pods in Pending->Running churned during the window.
Jin: could be SNAT/conntrack exhaustion. We've seen ephemeral client dials from init containers that open/close quickly when GPU drivers install.
Priya: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/apiserver -> conn_count, kv_cache_miss, controller_manager_leases. lease queue depth also rising.
Alex: paste of apiserver log snippet:
```
I0321 17:25:12.341 apiserver.go:123] http2: server_conns=1345 in_flight=320 p99_etcd=780ms
E0321 17:25:13.129 round_trippers.go:220] dial tcp 10.34.1.7:2379: i/o timeout
E0321 17:25:14.004 cacher.go:412] kvcache miss: key=/pods/default/worker-xyz
```
Maria: controller-manager shows lease-renew failures? last lease delay metric spiked.
Jin: yeah controller-manager log has repeated backoff while renewing leases — probably because apiserver tail latency caused operations to queue and then saturate watcher fanout.
Ryan: if this is tied to provisioning bursts, we need to decide between short-term NAT scaling vs longer-term fix (limit concurrent provisioning or batch throttle). NAT scaling costs $$$.
Maria: can we reduce apiserver load by enabling request throttling for provisioning controllers? maybe add a patch to the provisioner to backoff jitter.
Alex: quick mitigation: increase conntrack timeout & table size on nodes in eu-central and add a temporary NAT node to offload retries.
Priya: I'm worried about kv-cache shadowing: when many pods come and go, we invalidate prefixes causing heavy etcd reads. That explains kv_cache_miss and p99 etcd.
Jin: good call — snapshot compaction/IO wasn't high, so this is read amplification, not disk IO. Prefetch / local caching for provisioner might help.
Ryan: cost tradeoffs: spinning a NAT instance estimated at $1.2k/month but stops immediate SLO hits. Throttling provisioning reduces peak but prolongs onboarding.
Alex: propose runbook: 1) scale conntrack + add NAT node (mitigate now) 2) short-term patch to provisioner to limit concurrent driver installs (canary to 5% of traffic) 3) create follow-up to implement prefix-aware kvcache eviction and pre-warm list calls.
Maria: +1. I'll open SRE ticket.
SRE Bot: created ticket SRE-7893 "apiserver conn spike during GPU provisioning — mitigations + follow-up"
Jin: commands I'm going to run now:
```
# bump conntrack on nodes
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l region=eu-central -o name); do ssh $n 'sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144'; done
# add nat node
terraform apply -var region=eu-central modules/nat -auto-approve
```
Priya: I'll patch provisioning pipeline to add randomized jitter + max_concurrent=20 for driver-installs, will canary in staging.
Ryan: please add cost estimate to SRE-7893 and tag finance for NAT spend approval.
Alex: monitor channels: keep an eye on p99_etcd, apiserver.conn_count, controller_manager_lease_queue
Maria: noted. updating runbook with thresholds and rollback steps.
Alex: thanks all — ping if any regression. :thumbsup:
Jin: filing small follow-up PR for the provisioner in GH: https://github.com/redwood/provisioner/pull/204
Priya: added canary plan to ticket
Ryan: ack, will fast-track NAT approval if SLOs keep flapping
Maria: closing this thread in 1h if metrics remain stable :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Alex: agreed. good run.
